references.text: Aaron and his sons shall tend the lamps from evening until morning, which is connected to the incense offering that takes place when the lamps are tended.
Describes the altar of incense on which Aaron was to burn incense, providing the context for verse 7.
Gives the recipe for the fragrant incense (קְטֹרֶת סַמִּים) that Aaron was to burn on the altar.
Aaron shall tend the lamps and burn incense regularly before the Lord, a parallel to the daily service.
Aaron uses incense from the altar, showing the holy function of incense in the priestly service.
King Uzziah unlawfully attempted to burn incense, demonstrating that this service was reserved for the priests, such as Aaron.
Zechariah, a priest, burns incense in the temple and receives a revelation from the angel Gabriel, continuing the tradition of Aaron's service.
Mentions the golden altar of incense as part of the sanctuary furnishings, pointing back to Aaron's daily incense offering.
Incense rises with the prayers of the saints before God, a symbolic fulfillment of the incense offering in the tabernacle.
Connects the tending of the lampstand with the time for burning incense in the daily service.
Confirms that Aaron performed the daily service (the lamps) according to instructions that also included incense.
Historical confirmation from Kings that the daily rhythm of light and incense was observed.
Connects oil for the lights and incense as integrated parts of the priest's daily responsibilities.
